text:
maria: Customer (ACME) reports streaming sessions drop after ~32-38s. Client sees partial output then reconnects — they also observed duplicate billing events. They attached client traces and a minimal repro.

 tim: Can you paste the trace id + sample request? Is this hosted or dedicated?

 maria: hosted. model=gpt-neo-2.7b. trace=req_20260317_9999. Logs link: https://example.internal/logs/req_20260317_9999 (customer redacted).

 mike: Quick suspicion: ALB/proxy idle timeout mismatch vs client comment pings. ALB default idle is 60s but some proxies close earlier.

 sasha: Seen similar before — token refresh on client can block the event loop and stall sending comment pings, so middlebox/runtime thinks the client disappeared. If auth refresh triggers a 401 while in-flight, the server might close without a clear SSE close event. :thinking:

 ingrid: Also bring TCP keepalive into the checklist: proxy_read_timeout/nginx, ALB idle, and OS TCP keepalive intervals. We recently adjusted keepalive on dedicated; hosted paths still vary.

 support-bot: Repro steps customer provided:
```bash
# simple SSE repro
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>' \ 
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
They simulate token rotation at ~30s which blocks their client code path; stream stalls, client reconnects and immediately issues new request — billing shows two sessions for the same logical conversation.

 tim: Can runtime give us connection-level close reason (RST, FIN, proxy msg)? maria can you share the internal request id?

 maria: request-id: req_20260317_9999 (same as trace). Customer says client sees no error, just EOF on stream.

 mike: Pulled runtime logs for req_20260317_9999:
"keepalive: no data from client for 33s; closing connection" plus an auth-service response: "401 - token expired" at t+32s. So auth handshake overlapped the stall.

 sasha: Correlation looks strong. If client stops emitting comment pings during refresh, proxy/runtime may hit liveness threshold and drop. If auth returns 401 while connection open, runtime currently treats that as a failure and closes rather than emitting an SSE 'auth' event.

 ingrid: Root-cause hypothesis: synchronous token refresh on client side pauses comment pings -> proxy or ALB sees silence -> connection closed -> client reconnects -> new billing entry. Secondary: auth middleware response path triggers immediate close instead of graceful SSE event.

 jenna: Quick mitigations:
- Client-side: refresh token proactively (refresh before expiry) or continue sending comment pings during refresh. Provide this snippet for Node EventSource users:
```js
// keep sending comment pings while refreshing in background
setInterval(() => {\n  // send a comment ping line to keep proxies alive\n  eventSource.emit('message', ': keepalive\\n\\n');\n}, 10000);
```
- Server-side quick fix: increase tolerated silence window to 60s on the hosted edge, and make auth middleware emit a structured SSE event on 401 instead of immediate close.

 ops-oncall: For immediate customer workaround, recommend background refresh + 10s comment pings. Escalating to eng-runtime for config tweak.

 mike: Longer-term suggestions:
- Have edge send server-initiated comment pings every 20s so middleboxes see activity even when client stalls.
- Implement billing dedupe: if a reconnect within 45s contains the same conversation metadata, mark it a resume instead of new charge.
- Add 'event: auth_refresh' SSE support to allow clients to react without reconnection.

 sasha: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket with logs, repro steps, and proposed config change (increase edge silence threshold to 45s and add SSE auth event). Assigning to @mike and @ingrid for proxy/edge changes.

 tim: Also record this as a support KB article: "Streaming: avoid duplicate billing during token rotation" with code samples and server recommendations.

 maria: Customer will try client change first (background refresh + keepalive). I've told them we'll push an edge config change as well. Marking P1 since enterprise customer.

 sasha: Taking. I'll attach runtime traces and open PR for SSE auth event handling. :thumbsup:

 jenna: I'll draft the KB entry and the Node/Go examples.

 ops-oncall: Noted. If customer still sees duplicates after client change, we'll do deeper packet captures and consider rolling edge change behind a flag for the tenant.

 tim: Thanks all — keep thread updated with status and ticket/PR links.

 end of thread"
